The page gives only the mountain frontiers and six departments including Burgas; the Rhodope villages of the Republic of Tamrash are outside this reading.

region.text: Eastern Rumelia, "created in 1878 by virtue of the Treaty of Berlin", between the Balkan Mountains, the Rhodopes and Strandzha

ledger.note: 13 July 1878: the Treaty of Berlin creates the autonomous province of Eastern Rumelia under Ottoman political and military jurisdiction (Article 13), with Plovdiv as capital.

region.text: Eastern Rumelia, an autonomous province under Ottoman suzerainty

ledger.note: 13 July 1878: Eastern Rumelia "was created as an autonomous province within the Ottoman Empire by the Treaty of Berlin", "to remain under the political and military jurisdiction of the Ottoman Empire" with "significant administrative autonomy (Article 13)", under "a Christian Governor-General appointed by the Sublime Porte"; "nominally under Ottoman suzerainty until Bulgaria became de jure independent in 1908". The ottoman-empire dossier records the same relation (vassal_start 1878/7, vassal_end 1885) under the counterpart string 'Eastern Rumelia'; it should use the slug eastern-rumelia. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: added]

region.text: Eastern Rumelia under "Arkady Stolypin ... Russian civil administrator"

ledger.note: 9 October 1878: the Russian civil administration begins; the page does not call it an occupation, so the type is the researcher's reading.
18 May 1879: Aleksandar Bogoridi takes office as Governor-General and Stolypin's administration ends; the Organic Statute was adopted on 14 April 1879.

Eastern Rumelia "de facto ceased to exist in 1885, when it was united with the Principality of Bulgaria" (6 September 1885 O.S., 18 September new style); the Ottoman suzerainty stayed nominal to 1908 but the province itself no longer existed. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: added]

region.text: Eastern Rumelia annexed by the Principality of Bulgaria

ledger.note: 6 September 1885 (O.S.; 18 September in the Unification page's new-style date): "After a bloodless revolution ... the province was annexed by the Principality of Bulgaria." The Serbo-Bulgarian War followed.

18 September [O.S. 6 September] 1885: the Plovdiv takeover that ends the province; the Tophane Agreement of 5 April 1886 [O.S. 24 March] recognised the Prince of Bulgaria as Governor-General of Eastern Rumelia, a union kept until 1908.

certainty.note: Boundary fixed by the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878) and a boundary commission, though the page itself gives only mountain ranges and six departments; the Rhodope Pomak villages of the Republic of Tamrash, which refused its authority, are the exception.

notes: Cliopatria has no row. Seven years only (below the ten-year threshold of the brief) but flagged by eu-18-h as the counterpart of Bulgaria's 1885 gain. One keyframe. Gaps: the Berlin boundary in detail (page silent); the date of the Republic of Tamrash (about twenty Pomak villages refusing Eastern Rumelian authority; page silent); the Rhodope and Kresna-Razlog events (page silent); Kardzhali and Tamrash returned to the Ottomans under the Tophane Agreement of 1886 per the Eastern Rumelia page (the Unification page is silent), after the province itself had ended. The de jure existence to 1908 is noted but not drawn. Date convention: Bulgarian sources use Old Style (6 September); the Unification page gives 18 September new style. The Serbian counterpart is the dossier serbs (1804-1918, eu-18-f). Wikidata id null (unreachable). Review fix (2026-11-01): the dossier now records the autonomy as a vassal_start (1878/7) and vassal_end (1885/9) with counterpart ottoman-empire, confidence 3 on the page's words "autonomous province within the Ottoman Empire" and "nominally under Ottoman suzerainty"; the Eastern Rumelia page mentions no tribute. The Serbo-Bulgarian War (14 November 1885 to March 1886) is dropped from wars: it began after the province ended in September 1885 and belongs to the Principality of Bulgaria (the notes keep it). The ottoman-empire ledger (events 193 and 202) uses the string 'Eastern Rumelia' as counterpart and should use the slug eastern-rumelia; I do not own that file.
